title: Shift compatibility of open extension and restriction
statement: Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. For finite-type $k$-schemes $W$ with their small pro-etale sites put $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$, and let $\mathscr S_W$ be the abelian category of strict semilinear systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves, with its ordinary unbounded derived category, derived reduction $\mathcal R_W$ and total-limit functor $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; regard $\mathscr S_W$ as the module category of the ring diagram $((A_n)_W)_n$ on the simultaneous ringed diagram site of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. For a quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow W$, let $J_j:D(\mathscr S_U)\to D(\mathscr S_W)$ be exact termwise open extension by zero and $P_j$ restriction; $J_j$ is left adjoint to $P_j$, using the localized-site extension-by-zero adjunction of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] on the ringed diagram site. Equip both functors with their termwise cochain-shift comparisons. The unit and counit of $J_j\dashv P_j$ commute with every integer shift, naturally in the system complexes; the assertion is an equality of system maps before finite evaluation and total limit.

proof.text: The open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow W$ is etale, so $U$ is an object of the small pro-etale site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and the localized site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ is the site of $U$ used for $\mathscr S_U$. The ringed sequence site $\mathbf N\times W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ of [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site] has no single object localizing at $U$ in every level, so the localized-site lemma is applied level by level: for each $n$, [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] on $(W_{\mathrm{proet}},(A_n)_W)$ with the object $U$ gives exact restriction $j^*$ and exact extension by zero $j_!F=P_F^\#$ with $j_!\dashv j^*$. Both functors commute with restriction of scalars along $(A_{n+1})_W\to(A_n)_W$: restriction obviously does, and $j_!\operatorname{Res}F=\operatorname{Res}j_!F$ because the extension-by-zero presheaf $P_F$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] has the same underlying abelian presheaf for either ring, and module sheafification is computed on the underlying abelian presheaf [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], with restriction of scalars leaving the abelian sheaf unchanged [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Hence applying $j_!$, resp. $j^*$, to each level $M_n$ and to each transition $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}M_n$ defines exact functors between the strict semilinear-system categories. The levelwise units and counits are natural, so they commute with the transitions and form system maps, and the triangle identities hold level by level. This is the exact abelian adjunction whose termwise extension to complexes is the open adjunction $J_j\dashv P_j$ that [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] records on $D(\mathscr S)$ ('exact termwise $J_j\dashv P_j$'). Its derived unit and counit are therefore the images in the derived categories of the termwise unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$ of complexes, before any finite evaluation or $\mathcal L_W$.

proof.text: Write $e_1^{(a)}:J_j(X[a])\to(J_jX)[a]$ and $e_2^{(a)}:P_j(Y[a])\to(P_jY)[a]$ for the termwise cochain-shift comparisons. In degree $m$ both sides have the term $J_j(X^{m+a})$, and both differentials are $(-1)^aJ_j(d)=J_j((-1)^ad)$ by additivity, so $e_1^{(a)}$ is the identity of complexes; the same holds for $e_2^{(a)}$. These comparisons are compatible with $[a][b]\cong[a+b]$ and $[0]\cong\mathrm{id}$. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] the induced functors on derived categories commute with shifts, and their comparisons are the images of these identities under the localization functors. Unit square: in degree $m$, the cochain map $\eta_{X[a]}$ is $\eta_{X^{m+a}}$, which is the degree-$m$ component of $\eta_X[a]$. So $\eta_X[a]=e^{(a)}_{2,J_jX}\circ P_j(e^{(a)}_{1,X})\circ\eta_{X[a]}$ holds already as an equality of cochain maps, and hence in $D(\mathscr S_U)$ after localization, which is natural with respect to the shift comparisons. Thus $(e_1^{(a)},e_2^{(a)})$ is compatible with the unit, in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique], for every $a\in\mathbf Z$. By part (i) of that theorem it is also compatible with the counit (the same degreewise computation for $\varepsilon$ checks this directly). By part (ii), $e_2$ is the unique comparison on $P_j$ compatible with the unit for the given $e_1$, so it is the structure of part (iii). Both unit and counit therefore have the required shift squares for every integer, naturally in the complexes.

proof.text: All constructions in the preceding two steps are maps of the strict semilinear-system derived categories on the ringed diagram site. The shift equations are therefore equalities of system maps themselves; applying finite-level evaluation or the total-limit functor only transports these already-established equalities. This gives exactly the stated natural shift compatibility of the unit and counit of $J_j\dashv P_j$.
